claimMap.claim: Anthropic announced LSVP September 17 as a beta with more permissive biology access for verified research teams.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic announced its Life Sciences Verification Program on September 17. The beta gives verified life-science teams versions of Claude that allow more biology requests than general Claude.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Today, we are introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives life science professionals access to our Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet models with a refined set of safeguards more permissive for biology-related work.
The program is launching in beta, initially for teams and institutions.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Official September 17 announcement reread September 19; provider description only.

claimMap.claim: Anthropic says LSVP is designed for life-science tasks that generally available Claude models block.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic says the program is designed for life-science work that general Claude blocks. The closest alternative is general Claude with stricter biology restrictions; special access is unnecessary when an ordinary request already works there.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The LSVP is designed to enable life science professionals to use our models across a wide range of tasks that are currently blocked in our generally available Fable models

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Provider purpose statement; the ordinary-use alternative is a bounded editorial consequence.

claimMap.claim: Standard Use is team-wide and renewed yearly; High-risk Use is a project-specific six-month add-on that removes life-science request blocks while other safeguards remain.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Standard Use covers a team and renews yearly. High-risk Use is an extra six-month grant for one project that removes life-science request blocks. Anthropic says other safeguards remain.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: These grants can be extended to entire teams and are renewed once a year.

High-risk Use is an add-on grant for teams working in areas blocked under Standard Use. It removes all safeguards that block life sciences requests. This grant applies to a single research project and must be renewed every six months.
All other safeguards, such as cyber classifiers, will remain in place under LSVP grants.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Access structure as described by Anthropic; no independent safety evidence.

claimMap.claim: Anthropic says LSVP moves from request-time biology blocking toward monitoring patterns after activity, ties access to approved use cases and retains LSVP traffic for 30 days.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic says LSVP replaces immediate refusals with looking for patterns after activity runs. Access is tied to an approved use case. The company says it keeps LSVP traffic for 30 days so monitoring can happen.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Each entity’s access is tied to the use cases it has specified in its grant applications
LSVP shifts safeguards from real-time blocking to offline monitoring.
this requires 30-day retention for LSVP traffic

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Provider-stated design; effectiveness is not established.
